identity.description: Latent-attrition purchase model for non-contractual settings: Poisson purchasing while alive with Gamma-distributed rates across customers, and Beta-Geometric dropout that can occur only after a purchase. From an RFM summary alone it answers 'is this customer still alive?' (P(alive)) and 'how many purchases in the next t periods?' — without churn ever being observed.

axes.taskNote: UNCERTAINTY (U2/U3): no `clv` value exists in the 10-task union and BTYD is not `recommendation`. `regression` (expected future purchase count) is the honest nearest fit, with `survival` secondary because the latent dropout process is literally a survival mechanism. Proposal on the U2 agenda: a dedicated `clv` (or `latent-attrition`) task value for this family.

consumes.note: consumed VIA the event-log→RFM summary transformation, which is a SEPARATE Doc-2-placed component this family depends on (lifetimes.utils.summary_data_from_transaction_data). The fitter's true input is the per-customer (frequency, recency, T) triple — a tiny tabular summary, not the raw log. portTypeProposal (U2): an `rfm-summary` port type (specialized features:tabular) so the featurizer→fitter edge is typed honestly; today it is representable only as event-log-plus-adapter. targetSpec is `none` — the likelihood is over the event history itself; there is no separate label.

emits.note: conditional_probability_alive(frequency, recency, T) — the posterior probability the customer has not dropped out

conditional_expected_number_of_purchases_up_to_time(t) — expected transactions over a future horizon t; t is a predict-time argument, not a hyperparameter. lifetimes exposes the expectation only (the full predictive count distribution exists in the Fader–Hardie math but is not surfaced)

the fitted (r, α, a, b) ARE meaningful outputs (family truth: paramsAsOutput): r/α = cohort mean purchase rate, a/(a+b) = mean post-purchase dropout probability. lifetimes' summary exposes Hessian-derived SEs and CIs

the fitted transaction model is itself a consumable: gamma_gamma's customer_lifetime_value composition takes the MODEL object (not its scores). UNCERTAINTY (U2): whether every fitter implicitly emits trained-model or it must be declared per-sheet as here

penalizer_coef.note: L2 penalty on the four params; the documented lifetimes fix for non-convergence on sparse/low-repeat cohorts

invariances.why: sensitive in the INVERSE of the usual sense: frequency/recency/T are literal counts and durations inside the likelihood — standardization corrupts them; the only legal rescaling is a consistent time-unit change, absorbed exactly by α (equivariance). FLAGGED for U3: the boolean cannot express 'requires raw units' vs 'requires standardization'
log/rank transforms of recency or T change the exponential waiting-time structure the likelihood assumes; only linear time-unit changes are absorbed
the likelihood needs a complete (frequency, recency, T) triple per customer; the RFM featurizer emits complete rows by construction, so a NaN signals an upstream defect — reject, don't impute
the pure BG/NBD takes NO covariates at all — customer heterogeneity enters only through the Gamma/Beta mixing distributions
four explicit commitments: Poisson purchasing while alive, Gamma-distributed purchase rates across customers, geometric dropout after each purchase, Beta-distributed dropout probability
per-customer data is three numbers; identification comes from cohort breadth, and hierarchical shrinkage of sparse individual histories toward the population is the model's raison d'être
the fitted point process projects expected transactions over ANY future horizon t and P(alive) beyond the observation window — extrapolation is the model's purpose

featureStats.why: the dropout pair (a, b) is identified only from customers who purchased again — a cohort with few repeaters leaves attrition unidentified (degenerate or unbounded a, b)
variance/mean of repeat counts; the Gamma mixing exists to absorb overdispersion — a ratio near 1 says heterogeneity is weak and a plain Poisson would do
recency separates 'alive but slow' from 'dropped out' only when T is long relative to typical inter-purchase gaps; short windows leave P(alive) prior-driven

modelMetrics.why: expected vs actual transactions per customer over a calibration/holdout split (lifetimes' canonical validation) — the honest scoreboard for a model whose churn is never observed
predicted vs observed repeat-frequency histogram on the calibration period; a mis-shaped fit flags the Poisson-Gamma commitment before holdout error does

edgeCases.behavior: P(alive) ≡ 1 by construction — dropout can only follow a purchase in the BG story
edgeCases.note: zero-repeat-heavy cohorts overstate aliveness; route to pareto_nbd (continuous-time dropout) when repeat_rate is low

edgeCases.behavior: degenerate or impossible RFM summary — invalid likelihood contribution
(a, b) unidentifiable — flat likelihood in the dropout parameters
optimizer failure / diverging params on sparse cohorts (documented lifetimes issue)

driver.depNote: UNCERTAINTY (dep choice): lifetimes is in maintenance mode; pymc-marketing's clv.BetaGeoModel is the maintained successor but drags in the full PyMC stack and (under MCMC) a non-deterministic fit. Sheet is written against lifetimes; the choice is flagged for family-level review
driver.wrapperNeeds: the event-log→RFM featurizer is a SEPARATE upstream component (lifetimes.utils.summary_data_from_transaction_data); predict maps to conditional_probability_alive / conditional_expected_number_of_purchases_up_to_time(t) with horizon t a predict-time argument
driver.threadSafety: single-threaded fit; predictions are pure functions of the four fitted params — safe to parallelize after fit

canBeSeeds.note: the fitted BG/NBD is the transaction half of the CLV composition — gamma_gamma consumes it via its optional trained-model input

placementClaims.why: the RFM featurizer emits complete summaries by construction; a missing transaction is unobservable, not imputable — there is nothing upstream to impute
log/power transforms of frequency/recency/T corrupt the count/duration semantics the likelihood is written in
standardization destroys the raw units the Poisson/exponential machinery requires; only consistent time-unit changes are legal (absorbed by α)
no categorical covariates exist in the input contract — the pure BTYD model is covariate-free
